purpose: Teach: フェニックス/ユビキタス/フェデラー/バレンシア/ルックス/ゴッホ/スタンフォード大/寝たきり

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんがフェニックス神話の本を読まれた
lines.en: You know, when your father was young, he used to read books about Phoenix mythology.
lines.style: Soft, nostalgic gaze into the distance. Measured pace, as if retrieving a memory from a shelf. Warm undertone — not melancholy, but tender and deliberate.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん、お祖父ちゃん、ユビキタスって言葉に驚いてらしたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Yes, dear — and your father was so surprised when he first heard the word 'ubiquitous,' wasn't he?
lines.style: Gentle, conspiratorial tone as if sharing a private joke from decades ago. Light, affectionate — encouraging him to remember with her. Eyes crinkling with warmth.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんがフェデラーの試合をご覧になった
lines.en: When your father was young, he watched Federer play. Do you remember?
lines.style: Wistful, reaching back. Slight pause before the name — conjuring the image. Slower, quieter. The tone of someone offering a memory like a gift.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、バレンシア・オレンジを大事に召し上がってたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Your father was always so careful with those Valencia oranges he loved, wasn't he, dear?
lines.style: Warm, affectionate chuckle underneath. Teasing edge — the kind only long marriage allows. Lilting upward at the end, inviting him into the memory.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんはルックスよりお人柄でモテた
lines.en: Your father never relied on looks — people were drawn to his character instead.
lines.style: Quiet admiration in the voice. Steady, almost matter-of-fact — the confidence of someone who knew him well. Small, knowing smile underneath the words.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、ゴッホの自画像を愛されたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Your father loved Van Gogh's self-portraits, remember? He'd stand in front of them for the longest time.
lines.style: Soft, indulgent memory. Slow tempo, savoring each detail. Affectionate and a little sad — honoring something she watched him care about deeply.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お孫様がスタンフォード大に進学された
lines.en: When your grandson got into Stanford, you were so proud.
lines.style: Quiet pride settling into the words. Reflective, not boastful. A gentle acknowledgment of a milestone — still meaningful, still held close.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、晩年、寝たきりにならぬよう毎日歩かれたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: In his later years, you walked every single day, didn't you? You were so determined not to be confined to bed.
lines.style: Tender, proud — almost protective. Voice warm but steady, honoring his discipline without making it a performance. Close, intimate, as if reminding him of his own strength.
